summary: Tessa Wullaert scored twice, including an 85th-minute penalty after Georgia Stanway's handball, to give Belgium a 3-2 home win over England in League A1 of the 2023-24 UEFA Women's Nations League. England twice came from behind through Lucy Bronze and Fran Kirby, but Belgium equalised in first-half injury time and won late. A head collision between Alex Greenwood and Jassina Blom caused a 13-minute delay, and the result leaves Belgium second in the group.
one_line: Tessa Wullaert's brace, including an 85th-minute penalty, gave Belgium a 3-2 win over England in the UEFA Women's Nations League in Leuven.
key_facts: Belgium beat England 3-2 in League A1 of the 2023-24 UEFA Women's Nations League, played in Leuven on Halloween (31 October 2023).
Laura De Neve put Belgium ahead with a ninth-minute free-kick after Chloe Kelly was penalised for handball just outside the box.
Alex Greenwood and Jassina Blom clashed heads in the 18th minute, causing a 13-minute delay; Blom continued after concussion checks and Greenwood was stretchered off but was conscious and talking.
Lucy Bronze headed in Chloe Kelly's free-kick in the 38th minute to level for England, after drawing a foul from Marie Detruyer in the 36th.
Fran Kirby scored in the 44th minute after Lauren Hemp was released by Keira Walsh, putting England 2-1 up.
Tessa Wullaert equalised in first-half injury time, slotting into the far left corner after a counter-attack pass from Janice Cayman.
Mary Earps saved Wullaert's shot just past the hour mark after Wullaert beat Jess Carter and Millie Bright.
Georgia Stanway handballed from Yana Daniels' 83rd-minute effort, and referee Esther Staubli awarded a penalty.
Wullaert scored the penalty into the bottom-left corner in the 85th minute despite Earps diving the correct way.
Belgium are second in the group, one point ahead of England and two points behind leaders Netherlands.
Belgium host Scotland at Den Dreef, Leuven on Friday 1 December before a final group match away to the Netherlands.
England host Netherlands at Wembley Stadium on 1 December and need to win their last two games and hope Netherlands and Belgium slip up to qualify for the knockout stages.
